svg.aria-label: A sodium-glucose cotransporter carries sodium ions down their gradient and glucose against its gradient into the cell, while a sodium-potassium pump using ATP keeps sodium low inside
svg.text: intestine lumen (or nephron filtrate): high Na⁺
epithelial cell: Na⁺ kept low by the Na⁺/K⁺ pump
The pump uses ATP to keep Na⁺ low inside; the cotransporter uses that Na⁺ gradient to pull glucose in.
Glucose absorption in the small intestine; glucose reabsorption in the proximal tubule of the nephron.
